title: Research-quality fixture checksum newline portability v0
problem: The ticket-413 manifest stores canonical LF-text checksums, but the loader hashes raw working-tree bytes. After Git checks out fixtures with CRLF on Windows, six benchmark tests fail with checksum mismatches even though the text is unchanged. Ticket-414 must not depend on a benchmark whose provenance gate varies by checkout policy.
evidence: python -m rge.cli verify (6 benchmark failures after CRLF checkout)
acceptance_criteria: The checksum contract hashes canonical UTF-8 text with normalized LF newlines, and the manifest documents that canonicalization explicitly.
The same manifest checksum validates equivalent LF, CRLF, and CR fixture content while a substantive character change still fails closed.
Excerpt boundary validation uses the same canonical text representation as checksum and quote validation.
The focused benchmark suite and full mock-only pytest suite pass after a fresh Git checkout on Windows.
A follow-up pre-ticket-414 readiness audit records GO only after golden tests, full pytest, safety audit, and public-site build pass.
On completion, ticket-414 changes from blocked to ready; no later Phase 4 ticket is activated.
test_plan: With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/golden -q
With mock-only env: python -m rge.cli verify
non_goals: Do not weaken checksum verification or remove fixture provenance checks.
Do not implement the ticket-414 source-artifact classifier.
Do not change claim admission, database, retrieval, or public export behavior.
Do not run live LLM, source network, or cloud actions.
rollback_plan: Revert canonical newline hashing and portability tests, restore ticket-429 to ready, and keep ticket-414 blocked. No data migration is involved.
